doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Paul Mertz, 'Hurricane', and a photo of Bob Haggart
summary: Mertz's novelty solo and a song written under a different name, then a Chautauqua photo with Haggart.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: He’s still alive, he stroked and not very well. Paul Mertz wrote a thing, a novelty piano solo called “Hurricane,” which I’ve learned to play back in my early days, and also I found out later that he wrote a song which became quite popular called “In This World of Interesting People I’m Glad There’s You.” And he wrote that under the name of something else. And Jimmy Dorsey and he were the composer and lyricist on it. And somebody said that’s not right because it wasn’t Mertz at all. Well I found out that he wrote under another name. His middle name was his mother’s name and he gave that name as his name for that particular tune. But those are some of the trivia things. I’m not bringing these just for exhibition, I want to see them. There’s one picture, it was Bob Haggart, his wife and I had made at Chautauqua. It’s probably here. You remember this man from down in Chautauqua? Oh there’s Haggart and his wife.
Well I’m so glad that Bob is still healthy.
Yes so am I. He really worked hard down there. My goodness.
That particular weekend, he sure did.
